categories.title: Tool use
categories.description: Whether the firm knows which AI tools are in use and who may add a new one.

categories.title: Data handling
categories.description: What information reaches an AI tool, and whether anyone checks the output.

categories.title: Policies
categories.description: Written rules, a named owner, vendor terms, and a path for a bad paste.

categories.title: Training
categories.description: Whether staff have been told what not to put into an AI tool.

categories.title: Accounts and access
categories.description: Whose login is in use, whether access ends when someone leaves, and which devices count.

questions.prompt: Which description is closest to the business?
questions.hint: The report uses this only to tailor the last-page suggestion. It is not sent anywhere.

questions.prompt: About how many people work in the business, including owners?
Where does the business operate?
questions.hint: Select every state that applies. This quiz was written with small firms in Ohio, Kentucky, and West Virginia in mind.

questions.prompt: Which AI tools do people use for work, as far as you know?
questions.hint: Include free websites, browser sidebars, meeting bots, and coding tools. The DNS check and the browser extension look for a longer list than this question.

choices.label: Grammarly, QuillBot, or a similar writing tool
Otter, Fireflies, Fathom, or another meeting bot

questions.prompt: Do you have a current list of the AI tools staff use for work?

choices.label: Yes. It is written down and was updated in the last six months.
We have a partial list, or it is older than six months.

fix.title: Bring the AI tool list up to date
fix.detail: Ask each person which sites and apps they use for work, including free accounts. Date the list and look at it twice a year. The DNS check in this toolkit can confirm what the office resolver sees.

choices.label: We do not know which AI tools staff use.

fix.title: Write down the AI tools staff use for work
fix.detail: Ask each person which sites and apps they use for work, including free accounts. Date the list and look at it twice a year. The DNS check in this toolkit can confirm what the office resolver sees.

questions.prompt: How do new AI tools get into daily work?

choices.label: Someone approves a tool before staff use it for work.
People start using a tool, and it is reviewed later, if at all.

fix.title: Approve AI tools before people rely on them
fix.detail: Pick one owner. A new tool is either allowed for work or it is not. Write the decision next to the tool list.

choices.label: Staff pick tools on their own.

fix.title: Require approval before a new AI tool is used for work
fix.detail: Pick one owner. A new tool is either allowed for work or it is not. Write the decision next to the tool list.

questions.prompt: Do meeting bots or AI note-takers join client, patient, or customer calls?

choices.label: No, or only with notice to the other party and an owner's approval.

fix.title: Set a rule for meeting bots on client calls
fix.detail: Decide which bots are allowed, who may turn them on, and that the other party hears about it before the bot joins. Recordings and transcripts are client information.

fix.title: Find out whether meeting bots join client calls
fix.detail: Ask staff about Otter, Fireflies, Fathom, and built-in note-takers. Until you know, tell people not to add a bot to a client, patient, or customer call.

questions.prompt: What kinds of information have staff put into AI tools for work?
questions.hint: Select every kind that applies. If you are not sure, say so. A low guess hides risk.

choices.label: We do not know what people paste or upload.

fix.title: Find out what information staff put into AI tools
fix.detail: Ask a sample of people to walk through last week's tools and the kinds of text they pasted. You want categories, not a copy of the prompt.

choices.label: Public information only, such as marketing copy or published rules.
Internal operations, not client, patient, or customer information.
Client, patient, or customer names, or descriptions of their matters.

fix.title: Keep client, patient, and customer matters out of public AI tools
fix.detail: Tell staff that names plus a description of a matter, a return, a chart, or an account is enough to be a problem. Use an approved tool with a firm account, or do not use AI for that draft.

choices.label: Financial records, tax identifiers, or account numbers.

fix.title: Keep financial records and tax identifiers out of public AI tools
fix.detail: Returns, statements, EINs, account numbers, and similar records do not belong in a free chat tool. If a product is allowed to see them, that decision should be written down after someone reads the vendor terms.

choices.label: Social Security numbers, payment card numbers, or health details.

fix.title: Keep SSNs, card numbers, and health details out of AI prompts
fix.detail: Treat a paste of these as an incident even when the tool is familiar. The browser extension can warn on a managed browser. It cannot see a personal phone.

questions.prompt: Is there a rule that confidential client, patient, or customer information stays out of public AI tools?

choices.label: Yes. It is written and staff can find it.

fix.title: Write the rule on what must not go into an AI tool
fix.detail: One page is enough: which tools are allowed, what information is off limits, and who to tell if something sensitive was pasted.

fix.title: Write the rule on what must not go into an AI tool
fix.detail: One page is enough: which tools are allowed, what information is off limits, and who to tell if something sensitive was pasted.

questions.prompt: Does a person review AI output before it is sent to a client or used in a filing, return, chart, or customer message?

choices.label: We do not use AI output in that work.
Yes. A person reviews it first.

fix.title: Have a person check AI output before it leaves the firm
fix.detail: Name the kind of work that needs a human review: advice, filings, returns, charts, and anything a client will see. The person who signs the work is responsible for the words.

choices.label: No. Output is used as it comes back.

fix.title: Have a person check AI output before it leaves the firm
fix.detail: Name the kind of work that needs a human review: advice, filings, returns, charts, and anything a client will see. The person who signs the work is responsible for the words.

questions.prompt: Do you know whether the AI vendors train on your prompts?

choices.label: Work is done in accounts where training on our prompts is turned off, or we confirmed the vendor does not train on them.
People use free accounts and we have not checked.

fix.title: Check whether the AI vendor trains on your prompts
fix.detail: Open the settings for each approved tool. Prefer a firm plan that does not train on customer content. Free tiers often do the opposite by default.

fix.title: Check whether the AI vendor trains on your prompts
fix.detail: Open the settings for each approved tool. Prefer a firm plan that does not train on customer content. Free tiers often do the opposite by default.

questions.prompt: Is there a written AI use policy staff can find?

choices.label: Yes. It covers approved tools and information that is off limits.
A draft or a short email exists.

fix.title: Finish a written AI use policy staff can find
fix.detail: Put it where people already look for policies. Cover approved tools, prohibited data, meeting bots, and who to call after a mistake.

fix.title: Write an AI use policy staff can find
fix.detail: Put it where people already look for policies. Cover approved tools, prohibited data, meeting bots, and who to call after a mistake.

questions.prompt: Is one person named to approve AI tools and revisit the topic?

choices.label: Yes. A named person does this at least once a year.
It is shared loosely among owners.

fix.title: Name one person to approve AI tools
fix.detail: One owner or manager is enough. Their job is the tool list, the policy, and a yearly pass. They do not have to be an IT specialist.

fix.title: Name one person to approve AI tools
fix.detail: One owner or manager is enough. Their job is the tool list, the policy, and a yearly pass. They do not have to be an IT specialist.

questions.prompt: Has anyone read the vendor terms for tools that can see client information?
questions.hint: Where health information is involved, a business associate agreement is one HIPAA-aligned control among others.

choices.label: No approved tool is allowed to see confidential information.
Yes. Someone reviewed confidentiality terms, and a business associate agreement where health information is involved.

fix.title: Read the vendor terms for tools that see client information
fix.detail: Look for training on your content, where data is stored, who the vendor uses as a subprocessor, and how to delete an account. A healthcare practice should also ask whether a business associate agreement is offered.

fix.title: Read the vendor terms for tools that see client information
fix.detail: Look for training on your content, where data is stored, who the vendor uses as a subprocessor, and how to delete an account. A healthcare practice should also ask whether a business associate agreement is offered.

questions.prompt: If someone pastes sensitive information into an AI tool, do staff know how to report it?

choices.label: Yes. They know who to tell.

fix.title: Tell staff how to report a bad paste
fix.detail: Give one name or inbox. Ask people to report the tool, the time, and the kind of information, not to forward the sensitive text again.

fix.title: Tell staff how to report a bad paste
fix.detail: Give one name or inbox. Ask people to report the tool, the time, and the kind of information, not to forward the sensitive text again.

questions.prompt: Have staff been trained on what not to put into an AI tool?

choices.label: Yes. Current staff were trained, new hires hear it, and it was refreshed in the last year.
Once. New hires are not covered, or it has not been refreshed in the last year.

fix.title: Train staff, including new hires, on AI data rules
fix.detail: A short session is enough: approved tools, examples of what stays out, meeting bots, and how to report a mistake. Repeat it when you hire and at least yearly.

fix.title: Train staff on what not to put into an AI tool
fix.detail: A short session is enough: approved tools, examples of what stays out, meeting bots, and how to report a mistake. Repeat it when you hire and at least yearly.

questions.prompt: Whose accounts do people use for work AI tools?

choices.label: AI tools are not used for work.
A mix of personal and firm accounts.

fix.title: Move work AI use onto firm-controlled accounts
fix.detail: Personal logins leave the chat history with the employee. Issue firm accounts for approved tools and tell staff that work prompts do not go through a personal login.

fix.title: Move work AI use onto firm-controlled accounts
fix.detail: Personal logins leave the chat history with the employee. Issue firm accounts for approved tools and tell staff that work prompts do not go through a personal login.

questions.prompt: When someone leaves, can you turn off their access to AI tools used for work?

fix.title: Make sure AI access ends when someone leaves
fix.detail: Add each approved AI tool to the same leaver checklist as email. If the login is personal, you cannot turn it off. That is a reason to move the work to a firm account.

choices.label: No, or we do not know.

fix.title: Make sure AI access ends when someone leaves
fix.detail: Add each approved AI tool to the same leaver checklist as email. If the login is personal, you cannot turn it off. That is a reason to move the work to a firm account.

questions.prompt: Where do people use AI tools for work?
questions.hint: This checker cannot see unmanaged or personal devices. A DNS log only sees queries that use the firm's resolver.

choices.label: Only on firm-managed browsers or computers.
Also on personal phones or home computers.

fix.title: Decide whether work AI use is allowed on personal devices
fix.detail: Shadow AI Checker and a DNS log do not cover unmanaged or personal devices. If personal phones are allowed, the policy has to do the work, because the extension will not be there.

fix.title: Find out which devices staff use for AI tools
fix.detail: Shadow AI Checker and a DNS log do not cover unmanaged or personal devices. Ask whether work prompts happen on home computers or personal phones, and write down what is allowed.

questions.prompt: Where does AI chat history for work live?

choices.label: In firm accounts an admin can still reach.
In personal accounts the firm cannot open.

fix.title: Move AI chat history into accounts the firm controls
fix.detail: History in a personal login walks out with the employee. Use firm accounts, and decide how long history is kept.

fix.title: Find out where AI chat history is stored
fix.detail: History in a personal login walks out with the employee. Use firm accounts, and decide how long history is kept.
